Researchers made students wear an embarrassing T-shirt into a room full of people.
The students guessed almost half the room would notice.
Psychologists call it the spotlight effect.
You feel like everyone is watching. They're not.
If you've ever stayed quiet so no one would judge you, this is for you.
The question you didn't ask. The idea you didn't share. The gym you never walked into.
Here's the truth that sets you free.
Everyone is the main character of their own story.
They're too busy worrying about their own spotlight.
Even your nervousness shows less than you think.
Most people forget your awkward moment long before you do.
So stop living for an audience that isn't watching.
Ask the question. Share the idea. Walk into the gym.
You'll still feel the spotlight. Do it anyway.
Every time you do, the spotlight gets a little smaller.
Nobody is watching as closely as you think. So live like it.
Today, do one small thing you've been too shy to do.
